CITY COUNCIL OF MONTEREY PARK
  AND THE CITY COUNCIL ACTING ON BEHALF OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY OF THE
  FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
  AGENDA

  SPECIAL MEETING
  Courtyard by Marriott
  Boardroom
  555 N. Atlantic Boulevard, Monterey Park

  Saturday
  July 24, 2021
  8:30 a.m.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services
  to enhance the quality of life for our entire community.

Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located
at 320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and the
City’s website at www.montereypark.ca.gov.
PUBLIC COMMENTS ON AGENDA ITEMS
You may speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with
another person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor
and City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers.
Per the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting
please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a
meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair accessible.
This Agenda includes items considered by the City Council acting on behalf of the Successor
Agency of the former Monterey Park Redevelopment Agency which dissolved February 1, 2012.
Successor Agency matters will include the notation of “SA” next to the Agenda Item Number.

CALL TO ORDER  Mayor
ROLL CALL  Peter Chan, Hans Liang, Henry Lo, Fred Sornoso, Yvonne Yiu

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.3(a), the public may
address the City Council only on matters listed on the Agenda. Those wishing to speak on an
agenda item must utilize one of the methods listed above. No other public comment will be
accepted. To ensure the workshop begins and ends on time, the total time allocated for all public
comment, regardless of the number of speakers, is 15 minutes. If you were unable to speak during
this part of public comment, the City Council may, but is not required to, provide an opportunity for
such comment at the end of the workshop. Written communications will be provided to the City
Council but will not be read out loud.
   Monterey Park City Council and Successor Agency Agenda, July 24, 2021 - Page 2

NEW BUSINESS

 1.  STRATEGIC PLANNING WORKSHOP -
  This is a City Council workshop to prioritize the City’s legislative and project
  agenda. It is anticipated that the workshop will not result in the City Council taking
  any particular action. Instead, City Councilmembers and key staff members will be
  reviewing the City Council’s previous strategic plan; updating it; and providing
  direction to the City Manager. Topics may include, without limitation, infrastructure
  improvements; revenue enhancement; land use challenges; and municipal
  property needs assessment. Any direction provided by the City Council will appear
  on future meeting agendas. The anticipated outline of the workshop will follow this
  general order:
  •  Overview
  •  Lasting Community Impacts
  •  Refresher on Form of Government
  •  Review Work to Date for 2021, Explore Plans for remainder of 2021 and
  into 2022
  •  Headwinds: Change as Process, not an Event
  •  Hot Topics
  •  Strategic Plan
  •  Next Steps

ADJOURN

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JULY 24, 2021

The City Council of the City of Monterey Park held a Special Meeting of the Council at
Courtyard by Marriott, Boardroom, located at 555 N. Atlantic Blvd in the City of
Monterey Park, Saturday, July 24, 2021 at 8:30 a.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Yiu called the meeting to order at 8:32 a.m.

ROLL CALL:
Deputy City Clerk Trang called the roll:
Council Members Present:  Peter Chan, Hans Liang, Henry Lo, Fred Sornoso, and
  Yvonne Yiu
Council Members Absent:  None

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Ron Bow, City Attorney Karl Berger, Assistant City
Manager Inez Alvarez, Fire Chief Matt Hallock, City Librarian Diana Garcia, Director of
Management Services Martha Garcia, Director of Public Works Frank Lopez, Police
Chief Kelly Gordon, Director of Human Resources and Risk Management Christine
Tomikawa, Deputy City Clerk Cindy Trang, Secretary to City Manager Diana Wong, and
Moderator, Patrick Ibarra of the Mejorando Group.

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS
None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS

  - George Bocaregra, member of the Carpentry Union, spoke about the Workforce
  Development Program and encouraged the City Council to utilize local skilled and
  trade labors for projects within the City.

  - Jeshow Yang urged the City Council to prioritize policies around climate change,
  transportation, and housing.

  - Jennifer Tang talked about the Inclusionary Housing ordinance, community
  workforce agreement, disposable utensils ordinance, and the Spirit bus. She urged
  the City Council to prioritize policies around climate change, transportation, and
  housing.

  - Laura Gallegos shared the sentiments of other speakers and also urged the City
  Council to prioritize policies around climate change, transportation, and housing.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services to enhance
  the quality of life for our entire community
   69-172
  July 24, 2021
  - Calvin Truong spoke about the need for affordable housing and rent control. He
  urged the City Council to prioritize policies around climate change, transportation,
  and housing.

  - Edwin Sun urged the City Council to prioritize policies and spoke about affordable
  housing and climate change.

  - Kathy Ko urged the City Council to prioritize policies around climate change,
  transportation, and housing. She mentioned pedestrian and traffic safety and
  requested the City Council to revisit bike lane.

The City Clerk’s office received and filed eleven written communications urging the City
Council to prioritize policies around climate change, transportation, and housing from:
Andy Fung, Jeshow Yang, Austin Phung, Sarah Chang, Tara Kwan, Jimena Romano,
Ania Ty, Barbara Ngai, Connie Ho, Jean Park and Alison Silaphet.

NEW BUSINESS

1.  STRATEGIC PLANNING workshop

  This is a City Council workshop to prioritize the City’s legislative and project
  agenda. It is anticipated that the workshop will not result in the City Council taking
  any particular action. Instead, City Councilmembers and key staff members will be
  reviewing the City Council’s previous strategic plan; updating it; and providing
  direction to the City Manager. Topics may include, without limitation, infrastructure
  improvements; revenue enhancement; land use challenges; and municipal
  property needs assessment. Any direction provided by the City Council will
  appear on future meeting agendas. The anticipated outline of the workshop will
  follow this general order:

  •  Overview
  •  Lasting Community Impacts
  •  Refresher on Form of Government
  •  Review Work to Date for 2021, Explore Plans for remainder of 2021 and
  into 2022
  •  Headwinds: Change as Process, not an Event
  •  Hot Topics
  •  Strategic Plan
  •  Next Steps
   69-173
  July 24, 2021
  Discussion: Patrick Ibarra of the Mejorando Group facilitated a strategic workshop
  for the City Council to discuss ideas and suggestions towards the future vision of
  the City. The City Council ensued in discussions regarding Lasting Community
  Impacts; Refresher on the Form of Government; Review Work to Date for 2021,
  Explore Plans and Goals for 2021/22; “Headwinds: Change as a Process, not an
  Event”; Hot Topics including discussion on community, governance, economic
  development, infrastructure, internal/operational, environmental, housing,
  amenities, and public safety; Strategic Plan; and Next Steps to include climate
  action plans, housing elements, homelessness, tax ballot, public art, and
  community beautification and esthetic.

  Action Taken: No reportable action taken.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business for consideration, the meeting was adjourned at 3:20
p.m.

__________________________
Vincent D. Chang
City Clerk

  Approved on August 4, 2021 at the Regular City Council Meeting
